text:
finn: ran a 10k replay of short-query profile on staging. host CPU dominated by `parse/tokenize` + lots of tiny grpc writes. quick summary below.

rachel: paste the flame snippet?

finn: top lines from pprof:
  49.7%  ingress_thread  ingress::parse::tokenize_and_normalize
  21.4%  ingress_thread  grpc::writev_emit_small
   8.9%  ingress_thread  kvcache::lookup_remote
   6.2%  ingress_thread  http::frame::serialize

chen: yikes tokenize at ~50%. is this double work (gateway + host)?

finn: yes — gateway does optimistic pretokenize for some clients, but host still runs sanitize and re-parse for attach/stream fallback. found codepath that forces sanitize when attachments present. short requests without attachments still get reparsed in a couple spots.

mika: quick wins: (1) respect a gateway header for internal flows to skip host re-tokenize, with a fast validity check; (2) adaptive coalescing for small grpc writes to reduce syscall storm.

rachel: agree on header gate — internal tenants only. add a minimal validator on host: check frame-level invariants (lengths, checksums) before skipping sanitize. low risk, big win.

chen: about writev: current coalesce window is 1ms. bumping globally to 6ms reduced write syscalls ~40% in local sim but added ~4-6ms p50 for tiny requests. We should do adaptive: enable larger window only when small-write rate spikes.

mika: implement a token-bucket rate detector per-worker: if small_write_count/sec > THRESH then enable coalesce window W for TTL seconds. revert when rate drops. expose THRESH/W/TTL as tunables.

finn: ran quick sims: THRESH 400/sec, W=6ms, TTL=8s seems conservative — writev CPU drops ~45%, tokenize unaffected. will run more.

rachel: kernel-selector note: after kernel policy update, some nodes picked kernels that prioritize minimal decode latency but bypass merged-write paths in ingress, increasing syscall counts. kernel selector today scores on flop/latency; add a host_syscall_penalty feature so selector prefers kernels that keep batching-friendly IO paths enabled when traffic profile is short-request heavy.

chen: good idea. propose we compute a small metric from recent flame snapshots: host_writev_ratio = writev_cpu / (tokenize_cpu + writev_cpu). If host_writev_ratio > 0.2 and p50_seq_len < 64 then bias kernel score towards batching-friendly kernels.

mika: also add a preflight synthetic runner: for each candidate kernel run a 30s short-request workload and record writev_syscalls/sec and p50 latency. Cache that profile for selector.

finn: kvcache: repeated prefix lookups show up even though % is low. for tiny requests absolute cost matters. propose a per-worker small LRU memo keyed by prefix-hash with 512 entries TTL 10s to avoid remote kvcalls for hot prefixes. feature-flagged.

rachel: watch memory. instrument mem_usage, hit_rate, eviction_rate. Default 512 per worker seems fine but make it configurable per tier.

chen: action items:
- header gate to skip host re-tokenize for internal tenants + fast invariant check (finn)
- adaptive grpc writev coalesce detector with tunables + metrics (mika)
- per-worker prefix LRU memo for kvcache lookups (chen)
- kernel-selector score: add host_syscall_penalty and preflight short-request profiler (rachel + mika)

finn: i'll open the header-gate PR today, include unit tests for invariant check and a replay harness attach. will request canary slot when ready.

mika: i'll PR detector with metrics: small_write_rate, coalesce_active, syscalls_per_request. will add dashboard panels for quick triage.

chen: i'll prototype LRU memo, measure hit-rate on replay and add mem-pressure guards. feature-flagged.

rachel: i'll start the kernel-selector change doc and coordinate the preflight runner infra. want this staged so we don't flip kernels without telemetry.

ops-bot: note: canary slots free: 1 and 4. Recommend canary for header-gate once tests pass.

finn: timeline: header PR today, canary tomorrow. detector + LRU in parallel over next 48-72h. we should add perf-runner asserts: tokenize% drop >= 25% for short workload and writev_syscalls/sec drop >= 30% or p50 delta < +6ms.

mika: adding those asserts. also add a rollback criterion: if p95 latency increases by >10% revert coalesce.

finn: thanks folks. ping me if you want to run the replay harness — I have a lightweight tool that replays short-request mix and collects pprof. :thumbsup:
